chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Jamil, from Aban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that he
was asked about a man who bequeathed 'something' from his wealth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The 'something' in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one from six (1/6)'.

key_terms.شَيْ‏ءٍ: something (a specific legal term for a fraction of an estate)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of bequeathing 'something' from one's wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ambiguous term 'something' (shay') in bequests by anchoring it to the authoritative interpretation preserved in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), specifically identifying it as one-sixth of the estate. This ruling highlights the Shia reliance on the Ahl al-Bayt's exegetical authority to resolve legal ambiguities in inheritance law, ensuring consistency with the Prophet's tradition.
